output.summary: A tropical, spiny evergreen shrub or small tree believed native to South Asia, southern China, Southeast Asia, and Central and West Africa. Its drooping branches may bear straight or hooked thorns, although some varieties are thornless. The fruit ripens from light green to reddish brown and is eaten raw, cooked, candied, dried, made into drinks or preserves, depending on ripeness and location.
output.edibilityNote: Fruit is eaten raw or prepared in several ways; seed kernels are famine food, and Indonesian leaves are used for an infusion.
